existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `ClinicalImpression` is present in R4 but absent from the supplied R6 core package, producing a hard R4-to-R6 break for existing instances and generated APIs. The main migration concerns are resource-type rejection, loss of a single aggregate assessment container, and profile-specific mapping to other R6 resources. The top uncertainty is the absence of official rationale or a sanctioned ConceptMap.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is not a simple rename. Implementers should inventory R4 `ClinicalImpression` use, decide whether each record should become one or more `Condition`, `Observation`, `DiagnosticReport`, `RiskAssessment`, `CarePlan`, `Encounter`-linked notes, or extensions, and preserve provenance/linkage so the original aggregate assessment can be audited. Systems with generated R4 classes or REST endpoints must expect removed R6 resource-type support.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the core identity finding because the expected R6 StructureDefinition is absent, the R6 package index has no ClinicalImpression entry, and package-wide searches found no occurrence of the resource name. Confidence is medium for the replacement/mapping analysis because only local package artifacts were available; official ballot notes, JIRA, or migration ConceptMaps could identify recommended mappings not evident from the package.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
ClinicalImpression has a resource-identity break: ClinicalImpression resource is absent from the R6 core package. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 92/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.
